api.analyses-list.statement: GET /analyses (limit<=200, newest first, owner-scoped via PR.user_id) and a `pr` block (PROut) on GET /analyses/{id} were added as the smallest backend change needed for the dashboard history and analysis header. Both are additive; no migration was required.

artifact.storage.statement: Local filesystem artifact storage is for development only. Live deployments must store diffs and other durable analysis artifacts in remote private object storage, while PostgreSQL stores metadata, storage keys, checksums, sizes, and references; local and remote backends should share one storage interface.

evidence.note: Production requirement established after identifying that instance-local files are ephemeral and service-bound.

aws.resource-scope.statement: Limit AWS resource reads and changes for PRism to resources identified as belonging to this project. Do not modify unrelated or shared account resources.

evidence.note: Developer explicitly authorized AWS Agent Toolkit setup under profile prism with the boundary that cloud-service changes remain within PRism project scope.

aws.s3.artifact-bucket.statement: PRism artifact storage is provisioned in ap-south-1 by CloudFormation stack prism-artifact-storage. Bucket prism-artifact-storage-prismartifactbucket-ubri8x7giofh is private, blocks public access, uses BucketOwnerEnforced and SSE-S3, has versioning enabled and an HTTPS-only bucket policy; backend IAM role and application configuration are still pending.

evidence.note: Verified the deployed stack and bucket configuration after creation. This operation created only PRism's S3 bucket and bucket policy; it did not create EC2 or RDS resources.

benchmark.pilot.scorer.statement: The authored benchmark now contains a discount-boundary defect and a stale active-timer regression, scored by exact issue labels, evidence verification, citation accuracy, and latency. PRism measured both defects with correct citations after a targeted risk-prompt change; results remain directional because the corpus is small and human timing is not measured.

evidence.note: PRism now has a one-case benchmark pilot with exact issue-label scoring, citations, evidence-gate rate, and measured latency; expand the sample corpus before broad performance claims. The local prism database was reset to empty application tables at Alembic 0007.

The timer case first exposed a false negative, then passed after the prompt required tracing changed settings against in-flight work. Latest review of human-simulator#2 remained correctly empty because the actual patch clears and re-arms the timer.

bob.codex.workflow.statement: Use Bob IDE as the visible primary build environment for hackathon evidence: the developer drives Bob Agent/Plan modes, skills, and parallel subtasks. Codex serves as the technical driver for project architecture and implementation, with Bob as the build-time passenger/partner; work should be coordinated through shared repo files and bounded tasks, never duplicated edits.

bob.sessions.deliverable.statement: A bob_sessions/ folder at repo root is a required hackathon deliverable. Every Bob IDE task session summary screenshot must be saved there as PNG, named clearly e.g. prism_task01_db_skeleton_summary.png. One screenshot per completed task.

bob.skill.review-pipeline-build.statement: A Bob skill file was drafted at .bob/skills/review-pipeline-build/SKILL.md covering pipeline constraints, build order, coordination rules, and what Bob sessions must not do at runtime.

build.sequence.statement: Build in this order: DB/API skeleton and facts engine; evidence gate; runtime agent and fixtures; frontend with streamed progress; authored sample repo and seeded PRs; benchmark scorer; product polish; README/demo support and Bob session evidence throughout.

coverage.provenance.statement: Coverage evidence must come from a real run and match the analyzed PR head SHA. A CI artifact is acceptable only when its workflow run is tied to that exact head SHA; otherwise run tests in an isolated environment for the authored sample repo or report coverage as unknown and emit no coverage-gap claim.

evidence.note: Bob's suggested latest Actions artifact needs exact-SHA validation.

data.provenance.statement: All sample code, specs, and seeded PRs must be authored for this project; do not use client data, confidential or personal information, or scraped social-media data. Track public reference sources and check their commercial-use terms.

database.local.statement: As of 2026-09-25, local Homebrew PostgreSQL 18.3 runs on localhost:5432. A dedicated non-superuser prism role and prism database now exist; backend/.env (git-ignored, mode 0600) supplies the app URL, and Alembic revision 0001 has been applied.

evidence.note: Read-only inspection; no PostgreSQL settings or databases were changed.
Initialized at the developer's request; machine-wide PostgreSQL authentication settings were left unchanged.

database.migration.enum-creation.statement: The initial Alembic migration explicitly created PostgreSQL enum types, then declared same-named sa.Enum columns that created those types again, causing DuplicateObjectError during upgrade. Removed the redundant explicit type creation so table column declarations create the enums once.

evidence.note: Fixed while provisioning the local PRism schema; alembic upgrade head then completed successfully.

deployment.alembic.password-url.statement: Alembic config.set_main_option interpreted percent signs in URL-encoded RDS passwords as ConfigParser interpolation and printed the URL on failure. env.py now uses settings.database_url directly for migrations; the initially exposed managed password was rotated.

deployment.architecture.statement: Deploy the Next.js frontend on Vercel and the FastAPI backend on AWS EC2. Use a private S3 bucket for durable PR artifacts and hosted PostgreSQL (RDS is the recommended managed option); the browser connects to the API over HTTPS for REST/SSE, and AWS secrets/roles remain server-side. Exact database service and network/domain details are still to be configured.

evidence.note: Developer selected this cloud split; local filesystem artifacts remain development-only.

deployment.aws.live.statement: PRism backend is live at https://api.amaankhan.in in ap-south-1 using dedicated CloudFormation stacks prism-ip and prism-api: EC2/Nginx/Certbot, private single-AZ RDS PostgreSQL, existing private S3 bucket, and project-scoped runtime role; frontend remains on Vercel to deploy.

deployment.macos.appledouble.statement: macOS tar included AppleDouble ._*.py files, which Alembic scanned as migrations and rejected due to null bytes. Build backend archives with COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 and --exclude=._*, and remove existing AppleDouble files from EC2 before restart.

deployment.rds.freeplan.statement: This AWS account free-tier plan rejected seven-day RDS backup retention; PRism uses one-day automated backups with single-AZ db.t4g.micro PostgreSQL 18.6 and 20 GiB encrypted gp3 storage.

deployment.rds.prerequisites.statement: Provisioning PRism RDS through the scoped deployer required the RDS service-linked IAM role and DescribeKey/CreateGrant access to the account AWS-managed aws/rds KMS key; managed master password also uses the aws/secretsmanager key. These permissions are scoped in prism-deployer-bootstrap.

evidence.gate.contract.statement: The evidence gate accepts typed findings with an explicit claim type and citations, validates every citation against PRFacts, and marks a finding verified only when every citation matches the claim contract. Unsupported findings remain available in the unverified appendix; coverage-gap claims require a specific uncovered line, while unknown-coverage claims require a file-level unknown status citation.

evidence.note: Implemented deterministic pure-Python gate interfaces and validation.

facts.coverage.implementation.statement: Coverage facts are now fully implemented (supersedes facts.coverage.stub). LCOV and Cobertura XML parsers in coverage_parsers.py; SHA acceptance gate and provenance in coverage_intake.py; build_coverage_facts() validates artifacts via accept_coverage(). Files remain unknown when no artifact, SHA mismatches, or parse fails. Migration 0006 adds coverage provenance columns to the analyses table.

facts.coverage.stub.statement: Coverage status is always CoverageStatus.unknown in this milestone. coverage_facts.build_coverage_facts() raises NotImplementedError if a non-None artifact is passed. A future milestone will parse Cobertura XML from a CI run verified against the PR head SHA (see coverage.provenance constraint).

facts.engine.design.statement: Facts engine implemented in backend/app/facts/ as four modules: models.py (immutable frozen dataclasses), diff_facts.py (line-number extraction from PRBundle), python_deps.py (stdlib AST import walker), coverage_facts.py (always-unknown stub). compute_facts() is the sole public entry point. No LLM calls; no filesystem access by default. Python source must be passed via file_source_map; absent files produce no edges.

frontend.analysis-detail.review-report.statement: The analysis report uses in-place Findings, Evidence, Coverage, and Diff tabs within one bounded report panel. Selecting a verified finding opens its evidence tab, citation actions switch to Diff and focus the cited file/line, and coverage provenance opens the Coverage tab; no sticky evidence inspector or hash-jump navigation remains.

evidence.note: Observed on the supplied completed review: long raw Markdown dominated the first viewport, while the evidence inspector was positioned beside the PR header. Verified the closed/open description behavior in the browser.
Verified in the browser that each tab changes content without changing the review URL; an unverified appendix citation also opened Diff with its file expanded.

frontend.benchmark-impact.empty-state.statement: No published benchmark results or benchmark API data are available in the current frontend, so Benchmark impact presents a clear empty state and describes only outcomes PRism will report when measured data exists.

evidence.note: Added Benchmark impact to the authenticated workspace sidebar as part of the SaaS UI redesign without inventing numeric outcomes.

frontend.build.shared-next-dir.statement: Only one Next.js process may own frontend/.next at a time: a parallel session running next dev together with next build or next start corrupts generated chunks and can yield missing-module HTTP 500 errors. Preview against the existing :3000 dev server, or stop and coordinate the owning server before building.

evidence.note: Two sessions ran concurrently on frontend/: a parallel session's `next dev` on :3000 shares the .next dir, so a `next build` + `next start` from another session can corrupt the production bundle (missing ./682.js chunks, HTTP 500). Preview against the running dev server or coordinate builds; dashboard/page.tsx also gained a PullRequestPicker mid-session that had to be preserved.
Observed Cannot find module ./682.js from webpack-runtime. Stopping the exact dev process, moving the stale .next cache aside, and restarting dev regenerated valid routes.

frontend.design.color-theme.statement: PRism’s public landing page and signed-in workspace share a Brainfloss-inspired palette of warm off-white surfaces, dark ink, deep coral controls (#b9332d), and bright coral display/logo highlights (#ed5148); green, amber, and red/rose remain reserved for review semantics.

evidence.note: PRism’s shared visual theme now uses Brainfloss-inspired coral (#ed5148), warm off-white surfaces, and dark ink across public and signed-in screens, while green/amber/red remain reserved for review semantics.

frontend.design.monochrome-light.statement: The frontend uses a light monochrome theme (white/zinc greys, black pill CTAs, zinc-950 dark contrast sections; Inter via next/font). Semantic color is reserved for verification states: emerald=verified/accepted, amber=unverified/rejected, rose=failed/high severity, green/red tints only inside diffs. The old dark surface/indigo palette is retired; status pills, kargul-style landing structure (badge, huge headline, stats, dark facets panel, pipeline, FAQ, final CTA) are the house style.

evidence.note: Revamped at user request: previous dark navy/indigo looked vibe-coded. Structure modeled on kargul.studio (status pill, oversized tight-tracked headline, pill CTAs, dark contrast panel, FAQ, big CTA footer). Verified via segmented browser screenshots; visual-judge subagent was unavailable (provider-not-found), acceptance pass done manually.

frontend.design.review-workbench.statement: The signed-in PRism app uses a persistent workspace sidebar. The dashboard itself is a review workspace rather than a generic Overview: its primary review launcher leads, repository access is a sticky secondary panel on wide screens, manual URL input is progressive disclosure, and review history is a separate work area. Keep all example data explicitly synthetic.

evidence.note: Implemented the approved Review Workbench / Findings Register direction and verified desktop, 390px mobile, and the 654px app viewport. Replaces the earlier monochrome landing-led layout decision.
Reworked dashboard after the signed-in surface presented an oversized generic Overview and stacked unrelated tasks without hierarchy.

frontend.page-title.background.statement: Do not apply the workspace header surface color to every header: page title headers should remain transparent on the app canvas. Apply the light header surface only to the compact mobile shell header.

evidence.note: The global `.workspace-theme header` selector painted all page title regions as white cards. A dedicated `.workspace-mobile-header` class now scopes that surface to the mobile navigation.

frontend.sidebar.destinations.statement: The PRism sidebar links to purpose-specific destinations: Workspace → /dashboard, Reviews → /reviews, Repositories → /repositories, Benchmark impact → /benchmarks, and Method → /about. Review creation stays in Workspace; the Reviews page supports client-side filtering by repository, and analysis detail routes remain part of Reviews for active navigation.

evidence.note: The prior New review, Reviews, and Repositories links were dashboard hash anchors, so each kept users inside the workspace instead of opening its own page. Dedicated routes were added and exercised in the local browser.

Follow-up removed the separate /new-review page and sidebar item at the user's direction, moved review creation back under Workspace, and added a repository filter plus larger padding to review cards.

frontend.stack.statement: The frontend is Next.js 14 App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind in frontend/, cookie-authenticated (credentials: include) against the FastAPI backend on :8000. Live progress uses fetch-based SSE (lib/sse.ts with a 30s stall watchdog and polling fallback); citations link into a client-parsed unified diff (lib/diff.ts); tests are vitest + Testing Library run with `npm test`, typecheck with `npm run typecheck`.

evidence.note: Supersedes stack.pending: the stack was later fixed in plan.md (Next.js 14 + Tailwind, FastAPI) and is now implemented.

frontend.testing.jsdom-url-validation.statement: jsdom 24 enforces native constraint validation: clicking submit on a form whose type=url input holds a malformed URL never fires the submit event, so dashboard tests exercise client-side pattern errors with a syntactically valid but non-GitHub-PR URL instead.

evidence.note: jsdom 24 enforces native constraint validation on type=url inputs, so submit-button tests must use a syntactically valid but wrong URL (e.g. GitLab) to exercise client-side pattern errors.

gemini.response-schema.compatibility.statement: Gemini GenerateContent responseSchema rejects additionalProperties even though PRism's OpenAI strict JSON Schema includes it. Build the provider-specific Gemini schema by recursively removing additionalProperties while retaining local parsing and deterministic citation validation.

evidence.note: Confirmed against the live Gemini API: unmodified schema returned 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT; Gemini-compatible schema returned HTTP 200.

github.app.actions-permission.statement: To download CI coverage artifacts from GitHub Actions, the GitHub App needs actions:read permission. This is not yet approved; coverage artifacts must be supplied out-of-band (e.g. uploaded by CI via the PRism API) rather than fetched automatically. Do not add actions:read without explicit developer approval.

github.app.permissions.statement: GitHub App tokens retain pull_requests:read and contents:read. Analysis fetches bounded changed Python source at the exact PR head using contents:read; CI coverage arrives out-of-band through the verified GitHub Actions OIDC upload API, so actions:read is not required.

evidence.note: Updated after wiring source enrichment and OIDC coverage upload; GitHub App permissions were not expanded.

github.auth.statement: GitHub PR ingestion uses the PRism GitHub App's short-lived repository-scoped installation token with read-only Pull requests and Contents permissions. Interactive user sign-in is implemented separately through the same App's OAuth client ID, client secret, and registered callback URL; local sign-in remains unavailable until those OAuth settings and session/token-encryption secrets are configured.

evidence.note: Refined after reviewing Bob's ingestion proposal and current GitHub App documentation.
The API currently accepts a PR URL after the App is installed on its repository; an interactive per-user GitHub OAuth/connect flow is a separate future frontend/auth feature.

Verified local backend configuration after the client secret was added: all required auth settings are set, and GET /auth/github/login returns a 302 redirect to github.com/login/oauth/authorize with state and PKCE parameters.

github.installation.browser-navigation.statement: For an existing GitHub App installation, Add repositories must open the installation's GitHub settings URL directly because GET /auth/github/install auto-links the existing install and redirects back to PRism. First-time connections should use a normal browser navigation to /auth/github/install so its cross-origin 302 is followed reliably.

evidence.note: The repository connect control previously depended on a cross-origin manual fetch redirect. It now uses a normal anchor navigation; the shared dashboard helper also performs a direct navigation.

Verified the old Add repositories action returned to Workspace. The updated link now opens the specific PRism installation settings page; GitHub displays its normal reauthentication checkpoint before the user can manage repository access.

github.installation.existing-link.statement: When a GitHub App was already installed before PRism started its account-scoped installation flow, GitHub opened the existing installation settings and skipped the setup callback if no repository selection changed, leaving the PRism user-installation association empty. The connect endpoint now discovers an unambiguous existing installation via the signed-in user's GitHub token and links it only after verifying user visibility and App ownership.

evidence.note: Confirmed with the user's installed PR Review - PRism App: the database had zero installation links; after the connect flow update, the dashboard displayed the linked Amaan-Khan14 installation and the association persisted.

github.pr-picker.statement: The dashboard can browse open pull requests from a selected connected repository using a repository-scoped, pull_requests:read GitHub App installation token. The PR picker submits the selected PR's canonical URL through the existing analysis flow, while manual URL entry remains available.

evidence.note: Implemented an authenticated installation-scoped PR listing endpoint and repository/PR selectors; frontend typecheck and backend syntax compilation passed.

github.repository-listing.ui.statement: The Repositories page fetches and lists actual repositories from GitHub's user-installations repositories endpoint, grouped by installation account. Use the workspace's page-header rhythm and padded white panel, with loading, access-error, empty-installation, and empty-repository states.

evidence.note: Added a cookie-authenticated endpoint and dashboard repository list; Safari now shows Amaan-Khan14/codedocket and Amaan-Khan14/human-simulator for the linked installation.
Confirmed on the signed-in /repositories page: repository names and public/private status render under the account, and the page uses the standard shell header and padded panel.

llm.provider.statement: Primary LLM provider is ZAI/GLM (developer has API key). If ZAI does not support the required streaming/tool-call interface, fall back to Gemini. The thin provider adapter must be written so swapping providers requires changing only the adapter class, not the agent logic.

pr.ingestion.statement: PR ingestion accepts either a GitHub PR URL or a raw diff and normalizes both to PRBundle. GitHub URL ingestion now uses a configured GitHub App installation token with repository-scoped read access to fetch PR metadata, exact head/base SHAs, and the unified diff; analysis stores this identity alongside the diff artifact.

evidence.note: Refined after reviewing Bob's ingestion proposal.
Implemented in backend/app/ingestion/github_ingestion.py; migration 0004 adds persisted repository and revision metadata.

pr.spec.source.statement: Use the PR body as the default spec input for a fast workflow, while normalizing it into an explicit spec_text field and allowing a user-provided spec to supplement or override it. Author detailed PR bodies for seeded demo cases.

evidence.note: Recommended to preserve the brief's spec comparison while supporting real PR workflows.

product.scope.statement: The product is a routed, database-backed multi-page website with dashboard, PR brief and evidence, benchmark impact view, live streamed new-analysis progress, and About/How it works pages. It is not an AI-only review bot or a single-page mockup.

project.identity.statement: PRism is a hackathon product for evidence-backed code review of large or AI-generated pull requests. It aims to reduce review time and missed regressions by checking a PR against its spec, cross-file dependencies, and actual test coverage.

review.pipeline.statement: PRism runs facet-focused prompts over deterministic PRFacts and the raw diff, retries transient provider failures with a configured fallback, and validates citations against facts before displaying findings. It skips cross-file analysis when no dependency edges exist and coverage analysis when no uncovered changed lines exist; prompts require concise summaries, minimal causal citations, and API-contract checks for framework-dependent claims.

evidence.note: Benchmark and live demo update: an authored timer fixture initially produced a false negative, then the revised risk prompt found it with an exact verified citation. The connected human-simulator#2 diff correctly has no supported timer bug because its setter cancels and re-arms the active timer; the pasted prior JSON was codedocket#2 and included an unsupported lock-file-leak finding plus malformed coverage citations.

A Human Simulator run initially failed because Gemini returned an incomplete dependency citation for a facet with no edges. Skipping evidence-less cross-file work removed the failure. Final run of human-simulator#2 completed with no supported defects; the timer implementation already cancels/re-arms, and Electron radio items manage their checked state.

runtime.agent.statement: The shipped runtime agent is a synchronous/streamed, provider-swappable API-backed agent, defaulting to Google Gemini behind a thin adapter. IBM Bob IDE is a development-time tool and must not be a runtime dependency or human approval/queue step.

evidence.note: Default provider changed from OpenAI to Gemini; OpenAI remains selectable.

runtime.review.orchestration.statement: Analysis creation schedules in-process review orchestration that computes and stores PRFacts, runs four typed facets concurrently through the configured structured-output provider, verifies each citation against the facts, and persists verification results. Gemini is the default provider (GEMINI_API_KEY/GEMINI_MODEL); OpenAI remains optional via REVIEW_PROVIDER=openai.

evidence.note: Implemented the runtime review milestone using strict Structured Outputs and the existing ArtifactStore.
Updated after implementing the Gemini GenerateContent adapter and configurable provider selection.

sample.corpus.statement: The authored synthetic shop corpus lives in sample_repo/ and deterministically rebuilds one base commit plus six case branches/patches with exact citation lines and local LCOV coverage artifacts. The branches are published as PRs #1-#6 in Amaan-Khan14/prism-synthetic-shop; each remote base/head SHA matches artifacts/manifest.json.

stack.confirmed.statement: Confirmed stack: FastAPI (Python) + PostgreSQL local (SQLAlchemy async + Alembic) + Next.js 14 App Router + Tailwind CSS. LLM: ZAI/GLM primary, Gemini fallback, behind a BaseProvider adapter. stack.pending is now superseded.

stack.pending.statement: The implementation stack is intentionally undecided. Before scaffolding, propose a fast 48-hour stack for backend streaming, zero-ops relational storage, and a polished web frontend, then get the developer's confirmation.

storage.artifact.statement: Diffs and large artifacts are stored outside PostgreSQL via a pluggable ArtifactStore (local filesystem for dev, S3 for production). PostgreSQL holds only metadata: diff_storage_key, diff_size_bytes, diff_sha256. The backend serves artifacts through its own /analyses/{id}/diff endpoint; the S3 bucket is never made public.

storage.async.s3.statement: boto3 is synchronous; all S3 calls from FastAPI async handlers must be dispatched via asyncio.get_running_loop().run_in_executor(None, ...) — not get_event_loop(), which is deprecated inside a running loop in Python 3.10+. LocalArtifactStore calls go through the same path for consistency.

storage.diff.legacy-fallback.statement: GET /analyses/{id}/diff checks diff_storage_key first (artifact store path); if NULL it falls back to the inline pr.diff column (legacy rows). If both are NULL it returns 404. This makes backward compatibility explicit and correct.

storage.iam.statement: The S3 bucket prism-artifact-storage-prismartifactbucket-ubri8x7giofh exists (ap-south-1, prism-artifact-storage stack) but no application IAM role is configured. Before any live deployment the runtime must have a bucket-scoped IAM role with s3:PutObject, s3:GetObject, s3:DeleteObject. AWS credentials must never enter source control; use the SDK default credential chain.

storage.local.path-containment.statement: The original LocalArtifactStore._path used str.startswith for containment, which incorrectly passes sibling-prefix paths (e.g. /tmp/prism passes as prefix of /tmp/prism-evil). Fixed by using Path.relative_to() which correctly rejects any path not strictly under the root.

storage.orphan.cleanup.statement: After db.commit() raises, a fresh DB connection confirms whether any PR row references the stored key before deleting. Outcomes: no row -> delete; row found -> artifact kept (commit succeeded); DB unreachable -> artifact preserved, key logged at ERROR. Never delete without DB confirmation.
